brief.analysis: The single most important signal here is that measured against its own rising trend, defense is barely stretched—the raw reading (1.7) and the trend-adjusted reading (0.65) disagree by more than a full step, direct evidence the average itself is drifting upward, not that price is temporarily dislocated. Sustained global rearmament and higher defense budgets have genuinely re-rated the group, there is zero moving-average confirmation (0/3), and the nearer target is already essentially met—so the old flat five-year mean is an invalid target and the statistics are a trap.
brief.report_line: Avoid shorting defense-versus-S&P: the group has structurally re-rated on global rearmament, its underlying average is drifting up, and the reversion target is already met—this is a broken relationship, not a stretched rubber band.

brief.analysis: Chips have run ahead of the broader Nasdaq, and the strongest case for a permanent shift is the AI build-out: hyperscalers are spending on semiconductors at a pace that can keep this group richer than its five-year history for years, so the deep target that implies a 64% snap-back is a trap. The nearer target—back to the one-year average, about 12% away—is reasonable and hit in 6 of 8 past stretches, but the shorter-term trend still points the wrong way for a short, so put this on small and aim only for that nearer target.
brief.report_line: Short chips-versus-Nasdaq in small size toward the one-year average only; the AI spending cycle can hold this group expensive, so do not press for the full historical mean.

brief.analysis: Silver had run enormously far ahead of gold at the peak but has already snapped back hard—it has reached its one-year-average target and the trend has turned, so the confirmed reversion is real and most of the move is already behind us. Both metals have their own structural bids (central-bank gold buying, industrial and solar demand for silver), which caps how far the ratio should fall, so treat the remaining ~14% toward the older mean as optional rather than the base case.
brief.report_line: Silver-versus-gold has cleanly reverted and hit its one-year-average target; the trade is confirmed but largely played out, so bank the move and don't count on a return to the deeper historical mean.
